issues.step: W1-1 turn 10 (request_0011) report, after compare_media turn 4 (request_0005)
issues.what: E18 reports the sound differs at almost every aligned interval from A 35.0 s to 79.0 s (spectral similarity 0.23-0.4), but ASR was never run on the source E14, and the report then concedes: "The source soundtrack was not transcribed for a semantic comparison, so replacement speech, music changes and other explanations for the measured audio differences cannot be distinguished."
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the student to note a large audio alteration (about 44 s of the clip) and then call its nature undeterminable, when one cheap step (ASR on B, compared with A's E11 transcript) would answer it.
issues.ideal: After compare_media flagged the sound differences, run INSPECT asr on E14 and compare the B transcript at B 34.6-93.8 s with E11, so the report can say whether speech was replaced or shifted.

issues.step: W1-1 turn 10 (request_0011) F3, with frame steps turns 5-8 (request_0006-0009)
issues.what: Four get_frames calls were made to "provide visual evidence to assess the proposed cut", and turn 9's rationale even says "E25-E28 show the source's interview-to-end-card transition". F3 still only lists sampling times and disclaims them: "they do not alone establish what each paired picture depicts".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches gathering targeted frames and then writing a filler finding that draws no visual conclusion, so the frame steps go to waste.
issues.ideal: F3 should say what the paired frames show (e.g. whether A 43.6/44.0 s matches B 42.9-43.4 s before the cut and B 58.7-59.2 s after it) and cite them for that conclusion, or the frame steps should be dropped.

issues.what: The rationales cite "E16" ("E18 reports that E16's 43.1-59.0 s is skipped", "E18 flags E16 94.3-98.4 s", "R2's video, E16"), but no observation the W1 workspace saw in this rendering mentions E16. The frames were requested on E14, and E16 only appears later in the GIA state as "frame of video E16".
issues.why_bad_to_teach: Citing an evidence id the student never saw teaches it to make up ids.
issues.ideal: Refer to the source as E14/R2 (the ids in the observation), unless E16 is shown in the state's evidence cards.

issues.what: R1 (hTn6oyx7BF8) also matched 99% ("E1 0.0-43.8 s = this video 661.5-705.0 s"), which suggests a longer, possibly fuller source. It was never compared or dated, and the rationale never explains why R2 was picked over R1. The report only says "Another search candidate also contained matching footage."
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches picking one candidate without saying why and leaving a competing original unexamined.
issues.ideal: State why R2 was chosen (100% match with near-identical timeline vs a long video where the clip sits at about 661 s), or at least check R1's upload date to settle which came first.

issues.what: The limitation "No conclusion of silence follows from an empty or failed transcription" is boilerplate: ASR E11 returned 11 segments. The tool failure that did happen (turn 1 OCR "returned failed") is never mentioned.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches limitations that don't match what happened in the run and hides a real tool failure.
issues.ideal: Drop the silence limitation and say that OCR on E1 failed, so on-screen text was not compared.

issues.what: Turn 1 says "E3 and E8 show Emerson College Polling branding, and all four frames show Forbes Breaking News branding". Turn 2 says "E3 and E10 show Forbes Breaking News branding and an Emerson College Polling backdrop". The two disagree on which frames show what, and turn 2 does not mention that the OCR just failed.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: Inconsistent, templated descriptions of the same frames teach loose visual grounding.
issues.ideal: Describe the frames the same way each time, and in turn 2 note that OCR failed so ASR is the remaining text source.

issues.what: The verifier sent back two "unsupported_assertion/critical" issues, but the exported REVISED ANSWER is word-for-word the same as the original.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: Training on a 'revised' answer that ignores critical verifier feedback teaches that revision can be a no-op (or the verifier flags were false and the pairing is noise).
issues.ideal: Either change the flagged sentences or record why the verifier was wrong. Check pipeline logs for which assertions were flagged.

good_patterns: The S1 query ("Forbes Breaking News Emerson College Polling \"October surprise\"") is built only from visible cues: on-screen branding in the frames plus a phrase from the ASR transcript E11. No claim text and no outside knowledge.

It ran compare_media on the candidate before calling it the source, and all removed-interval and sound-difference times in F2 and the answer match E18 exactly (B 43.1-59.0 s at A 43.8 s; B 94.3-98.4 s at A 79.8 s; the six sound intervals).

Dates are scoped correctly. It says 'this upload' was posted 2024-10-05 and the first archive capture is 2025-04-02, with "These dates do not establish that this was the earliest upload", and the answer repeats "earliest publication is unconfirmed".
It treats the backward correspondence near the ending carefully ("does not independently establish deliberate shot reordering; freezing or repetition near the ending remains a possible explanation").
cannot_judge: The images themselves (E3/E5/E8/E10, E19-E30) are not visible, so I cannot check whether the branding claims and the 'interview-to-end-card transition' description are accurate.

The E18 summary is cut off ('…(6 more not shown)' / 'Order differs: at A 81.3 s,…[truncated]'), so I cannot verify 'moves backward from B 99.4 s to B 98.4 s' or whether E18 explicitly reports the frozen tail (A 79.8-88.7 s per content_match) that the answer does not name.
Whether E16 appears in the W1 state's evidence cards (the rendering only says 'evidence cards also include source materials and metadata').
What the two critical verifier issues were, and what the GIA READ_RECORD E24 returned.
summary: This is a clean, short A-family run. A text query built from frame branding and ASR wording found the original (R2), compare_media ran before any conclusion, removed intervals and sound differences were copied accurately, and dates were correctly scoped to this upload. The main teaching risk is the audio: large measured sound differences (A 35-79 s) were left unexplained because the source was never transcribed, and the report says so instead of taking that step. Smaller issues are a frame-listing filler finding that draws no visual conclusion, rationales citing an unseen id 'E16', R1 left unexamined, a boilerplate limitation, and a 'revised' answer identical to the original despite two critical verifier flags.
